Daniel Sponov, son of Breyne and Hananya, was born in 1904 in the city of Baku in the Caucasus, Russia, and came to Eretz Israel with his parents in 1908. The family settled in Petah Tikva, and Daniel studied there at the Talmud Torah.

During World War I, the entire family was among those deported to Egypt. When they returned to Eretz Israel, they settled again in Petah Tikva. In the moshava, he served as a watchman of orchards on behalf of the local council. In 1926 he married. On the 26th of Sivan 5688 (13 June 1928), while on night watch, he was killed by stab wounds and was brought to rest in the cemetery of Petah Tikva. He left behind a pregnant wife and a son. The son who was born after his death was named after him: Daniel.

The circumstances of his death are described in the book "Reshit – LeMalot Shivim Shana LePetah Tikva" (First: On the Seventieth Anniversary of Petah Tikva).
